messages:
jess (support): @channel multiple customers escalating 503s / gateway timeouts against Hosted Inference in eu1 (eu-west1a/b). Started ~21:50 UTC, spike around 22:10. Examples: CS-4891, CS-4895. Sample curl reproduction -> 503. Request IDs: req=abc123, req=def456. Posting logs shortly.
ryan (oncall-sre): Looking. Are these all eu1? Any pattern by model/route? Can you paste one full request-id trace and the gateway logs around it?
jess (support): All eu1. One repro seq:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.ai/v1/hosts/infer -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-3.5-inf","prompt":"hello"}'
# -> HTTP/1.1 503 Service Unavailable
# x-request-id: abc123
```
Gateway logs show repeated upstream transport errors and "connection reset by peer" for upstream edge-pool nodes.
ops-bot: Incident created INC-2026-274 :rotating_light: (severity P2) - auto-assign oncall
ana (netops): I pulled SNMP/counters from our eu1 edge egress. Observed high retransmit and drop counters on the SlimPath peering (peer-as 64512) during 21:45-22:25. BGP chatter noted + short as-path changes. Also seeing large TX queues and fragmented packets (MTU mismatch) on the transit link, which correlates with reset patterns in TCP flows. Suspect provider-side microbursts + MTU/path fragmentation causing TCP resets to upstream model servers (long-lived connections for KV/cache fetches).
ryan (oncall-sre): Can you paste the tcpdump snippet and the AS path? If we can push traffic to backup transit (telia) that should relieve it quickly.
ana (netops): tcpdump excerpt (filtered):
```
22:10:12.123 IP host edge1 > peer  TCP 1514 > 443: Flags [P], seq 123:1671, ack 1, win 64240, length 1548  # lots of fragmentation
22:10:12.124 IP peer > edge1 TCP 443 > 1514: Flags [R], seq 1, ack 1671, win 0
# retransmit counters + ifconfig shows tx_queue_len spike
```
AS path: us->core->SlimPath(AS64512)->internet. I'm starting a manual route preference flip to Telia (AS32934) for eu1 egress now.
jess (support): Customer impact: CS-4891 on call, they reported timeouts in production during peak user flows. They requested ETA/mitigation.
maria (acct-exec): Pls give ETA so I can update the customer call. Their SLA window is 22:00-23:00 UTC.
vikram (eng-runtime): On the runtime side: we can toggle shorter upstream timeouts and increase client-side retries briefly to mask the flakiness (exponential backoff), and also rollout a small canary to fail to smaller model-variant with shorter sequence lengths to reduce chance of long-lived upstream connections. Will prepare canary config. Also adding prefix caching to reduce KV fetch count for repeated prompts.
deploy-bot: Deploy started: runtime/edge-config -> canary (eu1) by vikram at 22:26 UTC
ana (netops): BGP preference flipped to Telia via route-policy (prepended SlimPath, prefer Telia). Commands run:
```
set policy route PREF-TELEIA permit 10
  set local-preference 200
commit
```
Expect propagation within ~2-5m.
ryan (oncall-sre): Observing metrics: error_rate(api.gateway.eu1) dropped from ~8% to ~0.8% within 6 minutes of the route change. Long-context requests still see occasional 503s (0.2%)—likely leftover in-flight connections and fragmented flows.
jess (support): Notifying customers: CS-4891 updated, CS-4895 updated. They acknowledged the mitigation and asked for postmortem.
vikram (eng-runtime): Canary pushed: shorter upstream read timeout = 6s (was 20s), retry policy = [100ms, 300ms, 900ms], fallback variant enabled (gpt-small). Early telemetry shows reduced per-request upstream bytes and fewer long TCP sessions.
ana (netops): Full failover completed at 22:31 UTC. SlimPath still showing intermittent drops; we're keeping Telia primary for now. Continuing to monitor.
ryan (oncall-sre): Confirmed service recovery: 22:35 UTC 503s dropped to baseline. Will keep elevated monitoring for 2 hrs. Opening follow-ups:
- runbook update for multi-provider failover
- alert for egress retransmit rate > 0.5% for >5m
- add synthetic probe across both providers
maria (acct-exec): Thanks — I've scheduled a post-incident call with CS-4891 at 09:00 CET tomorrow. I'll include the mitigation notes.
jess (support): Closing customer-facing updates. Will attach logs and timeline to tickets.
ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-274 marked resolved at 1717533600 (22:39 UTC) :white_check_mark:
vikram (eng-runtime): Post-incident notes (to-do): 1) vendor SLA review with SlimPath, 2) automate BGP preference failover in runbook, 3) add egress health metrics to the console, 4) consider MTU mismatch detection at edge to prevent fragmentation.
ryan (oncall-sre): Good catch from netops. We'll file a blameless postmortem and include a timeline + repro (tcpdump + gateway traces). Thanks everyone for quick coordination :eyes:.
jess (support): Marking this thread for PM/CS follow-up. :phone:
